summary:
Mars Station Program is a pixel-art Mars survival and mission-planning game built in the Estella engine with TypeScript and optional Google Gemini support. Players pick 4 astronauts from a 6-member NASA and JAXA-inspired roster, pack a 24-cell (6x4) rover cargo bay, invest Research Points across a 4-branch upgrade tree, and run daily station and rover operations across 4 missions, including a 5-Sol guided tutorial and a 22-Sol ice-drilling expedition at -90°C.

Designed for the Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge, the game turns real mission constraints into hands-on decisions. An interactive coach named A.R.I.E.S. guides younger players step by step through crew roles, spatial packing, storm shelter protocols, and resource budgets covering Power, Food, Water, O2, Radiation, and Morale. Each briefing connects gameplay to real NASA missions and instruments, including Perseverance, Phoenix, and MOXIE.

Real space missions depend on strict mass, power, and crew safety trade-offs long before launch. Giving students a replayable simulator with immediate feedback lets them practice mission engineering and see how astronauts manage life support under pressure.

Link to How to Play: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1sbTsRdjiAR1-CI4az3n5EhOXfOdUhRH_/view?usp=drive_link

Introduction

Mars Station Program is a pixel-art Mars survival and mission-planning game where players manage a 4-astronaut crew from pre-launch preparation to surface operations and safe return. Before launch, players choose 4 astronauts from a 6-member roster inspired by real NASA and JAXA astronauts: Neil Armstrong, Eileen Collins, Kalpana Chawla, Bernard Harris Jr., Chiaki Mukai, and Scott Kelly. Each astronaut brings a role affinity (30% fewer supplies, 50% faster work, and 15% higher yield on matching tasks) plus a once-per-mission signature ability such as Field Fabrication or Germination Tray. Between missions, players invest Research Points across a 4-branch upgrade tree covering Infrastructure, Survival, Operations, and Crew, with 6 nodes per branch.

Between missions, players spend Research Points (starting with 3 RP, with full refunds available anytime) across a 4-branch upgrade tree with 6 nodes per branch across 4 tiers (3, 5, 7, and 10 RP). Infrastructure boosts solar generation, cuts power drain, and unlocks Battery Bank and Habitat Microgrid for indoor Life Support during storms. Survival lowers food and water upkeep, boosts plant yields, and unlocks Emergency Electrolysis and Emergency Stores. Operations improves rover yields, speeds up tasks, and unlocks Weather Relay (revealing exact storm dates from Sol 1) and Autonomous Recorder (protecting survey progress through a lost Sol). Crew slows morale loss, adds radiation shielding, and unlocks Cross-Training and Protected Rotation.


Before departing, players pack a 24-cell (6x4) rover cargo bay by dragging and rotating items through 4 orientations (R to rotate, Esc or click to remove, or Auto Fill for quick setup). Each mission requires a dedicated instrument: the Wind Sampler (2x2) for Tharsis Ridge Weather Survey, the RAD Detector (1x2) for Radiation Detective, or the Ice Drill (1x3) for Ice Hunter. Players fit that instrument alongside life-support cargo including Extra Rations (2x1), Water Canister (1x2), Oxygen Tank (3x1), an L-shaped Repair Kit (3 cells), Battery Pack (2x1), Seed Pod (1x1), and Medkit (1x1). Live Food, Water, and O2 meters on the right verify whether the packed load sustains 4 astronauts through the mission deadline.

Spatial Cargo Preparation and Four Missions

Players progress through 4 missions with escalating hazards. Tharsis Training Run (Tutorial, Sol 5) offers mild weather and a 24-hour weather objective at Training Marker while A.R.I.E.S. highlights each button step by step. Tharsis Ridge Weather Survey (Easy, Sol 20) requires 48 hours of weather data at Site A amid regional dust storms at -58°C. Radiation Detective (Medium, Sol 20) sends the rover to Hawksbill Gap for 72 hours of readings through a solar particle storm window. Ice Hunter (Hard, Sol 22) pushes players to Jezero Crater Rim to drill 48 hours of ice cores in -70°C to -90°C cold and heavy storm pressure.


Daily Station Loop and Rover Expeditions

On Mars, gameplay splits across two views: Station and Expedition. Each Sol begins with a morning briefing pulled from 10 unique Sol 1 landing events and 36 randomized station and rover events scaled to current weather and mission stage. Players then schedule jobs across Rover Bay, Instrument Lab, Life Support, and Storage using two-step Lock lead assignment while managing Power, Food, Water, O2, Materials, Radiation, and Morale. On the Expedition side, players assign 2 travelers to drive the rover to the field site, deploy instruments, collect science hours, and dock back at the station before the Sol deadline. Before advancing the day, an End Sol safety check flags unscheduled jobs or critical supply shortages, and animated crew report cards summarize each astronaut's HP, morale, and task progress after the Sol resolves.

Benefits, Intended Impact, and Accessibility

Spaceflight engineering depends on strict mass, volume, power, and crew safety trade-offs long before launch. Mars Station Program turns those constraints into hands-on decisions for students and junior astronauts. Instead of memorizing static facts, players see why an L-shaped Repair Kit displaces an Oxygen Tank, why dust storms require shelter protocols, and how cross-training or recycling upgrades buy extra Sols. Every mission briefing ties gameplay to real NASA and JAXA history, including Perseverance, Phoenix, MOXIE, LCROSS, Opportunity, Veggie, and DONKI space weather data. To keep younger players oriented without clutter, A.R.I.E.S. provides a clickable Next step guide, plain-language crew ability hints, and live work-order brainstorming.

Tools, Languages, and Technical Design

We built Mars Station Program in Estella Editor 0.104.1 using TypeScript 5.9, Node.js, and esbuild for Web export. The A.R.I.E.S. coach integrates Google Gemini (@google/genai) through a local Node.js API bridge (/api/gemini-plan) and falls back automatically to a deterministic local event and advice library when offline. Our art and audio pipeline combines custom Python scripts for procedural pixel-art sprites, animated walking crew, and synthesized UI sound effects with Pixelify Sans, IBM Plex Mono, and CC0/CC-BY-4.0 space audio.
